results.reply:
**Your legal position:**
Bhai, bina written agreement ke bhi aapka case mazboot hai kyunki WhatsApp par hui baatcheet ek 'implied contract' (maana hua samjhauta) maani jaati hai. Landlord sirf apni marzi se deposit nahi rok sakta; agar unhone notice period ka claim kiya hai, toh unhe ye saabit karna hoga ki notice period kitna tha aur aapne wo nahi diya. WhatsApp par aapke paas jo bhi proof hai, wo court mein kaam aayega.

**Law you can cite:**
* **Section 73, Indian Contract Act, 1872:** Agar koi contract todta hai, toh aap nuksan ki bharpayi (deposit refund) maang sakte hain.
* **Article 55, Limitation Act, 1963:** Aapke paas apna paisa recover karne ke liye 3 saal ka samay hota hai, isliye abhi kaafi waqt hai.

**What to do now:**
1. **Formal Demand:** WhatsApp par ek saaf message bhejiye jismein aapne kab room chhoda aur kitna paisa baki hai, uska zikr ho. Unhe 7 din ka time dein.
2. **Legal Notice:** Agar wo nahi maante, toh ek formal legal notice bhejiye (main ismein aapki madad kar sakta hoon).
3. **DLSA:** Agar phir bhi baat na bane, toh Pune ke District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) mein pre-litigation mediation ke liye apply karein (Helpline: 15100).

**I need from you:**
1. Kya aapke paas bank transfer ya UPI ka proof hai ki aapne 15,000 deposit diya tha?
2. Kya aapne room chhodne se pehle unhe koi bhi message ya verbal notice diya tha?

citations.title: Compensation for breach of contract
citations.plain: If someone breaks a contract with you, you can claim money for the loss it caused. The loss must be one that naturally follows from the breach, or one both sides knew was likely when they made the contract. Remote or indirect losses are not covered. This is the basis for claiming back an unpaid deposit, rent or salary owed under a contract.

citations.title: 3 years to sue for compensation for breach of contract
citations.plain: A suit for compensation for breach of a contract (written or implied), where no other article covers it specifically, must be filed within 3 years. Time runs from the date of the breach. If there are repeated breaches, it runs from the breach you sue on; if the breach is continuing, from when it stops.

citations.title: Pre-litigation settlement through Lok Adalat
citations.plain: Even before filing a case, one party can apply to the District or State Legal Services Authority to have a civil dispute, or a compoundable criminal matter, referred to a Lok Adalat for amicable settlement. Non-compoundable offences are excluded. This is available now, unlike Mediation Act section 5.
